title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes study a profinite group M. It is an extension of a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group gamma_{rho,sigma} (identified with Gamma_Q-tilde) by a profinite group written S^+-hat. S^+-hat looks like the profinite completion of the modular group, or a variant containing Pi-hat (the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}) as a normal subgroup with quotient S_3. Here sigma and rho are the torsion elements of order 2 and 3. N^*_sigma and N^*_rho are their 'normalisers' in M. L_sigma and L_rho are the corresponding centralisers or normalisers inside S^+-hat. The previous page showed two things: Gamma_{rho,sigma} ≅ M^!_0[0]/L_0^{Pi_0}, and the extension 1 -> L_sigma -> N^*_sigma -> Gamma_{rho,sigma} -> 1 splits. It also defined M^! = M(0).Pi and its index-2 subgroup M^!_0 = M(0).Pi_0, where M(0) is the subgroup attached to the (tangential) base point at 0.

This page:
- (136) M^! ≅ M^!_0 × mu, with mu = {±1} central, presumably the centre of the SL_2-type group.
- (137) N^{*!}_{sigma,0} := N^*_sigma ∩ M^!_0 and N^{*!}_sigma := N^*_sigma ∩ M^! = N^{*!}_{sigma,0} × mu.
- (138) N^{*!}_{sigma,0} maps isomorphically onto gamma_{rho,sigma} = Gamma_Q-tilde.
- (139) This subgroup is named M(1/2).

The notation is suggestive. M(x) is the 'Galois section' attached to the point x of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}:
- M(0) is attached to the tangential point at 0.
- M(1/2) is attached to lambda = 1/2, the Q-rational fixed point of the involution lambda -> 1 - lambda. Its orbit {-1, 2, 1/2} is the j = 1728 point.
- On the next page, M(-J) is attached to lambda = -j = e^{i pi/3}, the fixed point of the order-3 symmetry. That point is defined only over Q(sqrt(-3)).

The section M(1/2) splits all relevant extensions as semidirect products (140):
- M^!_0 = M(1/2).Pi_0
- M^! = M(1/2).Pi
- M = M(1/2).S^+-hat
- N^*_sigma = M(1/2).L_sigma

A marginal warning says M^! is normal in M and M^!_0 is normal in M^!, but M^!_0 is not normal in M.

The bracketed part (141) starts the analogous analysis for rho. It defines N^{*!}_{rho,0} = N^*_rho ∩ M^!_0 as the set of v in N^*_rho such that alpha v lies in M(0) for some alpha in Pi_0. For u in M(0) and alpha with alpha^{-1}u in N^*_rho, one needs u(rho) to be conjugate to rho^{epsilon_3}. Since images in S_3 = S^+/Pi must match, epsilon_3(u) = 1. Here epsilon_3 is the quadratic character cutting out Q(sqrt(-3)).

This leads to the next page's Proposition. N^{*!}_{rho,0} injects into gamma_{rho,sigma} with image the index-2 subgroup Gamma' = {epsilon_3 = 1}. This gives the section M(-J) over Gamma', i.e. over Gal(Q-bar/Q(sqrt(-3))).

In modern terms: inside a GT-like automorphism group of the profinite tripod/modular tower, Grothendieck builds combinatorial analogues of the Galois sections attached to rational points. The point 1/2 gives a section over the whole group. The point e^{i pi/3} gives a section only over the index-2 'Q(sqrt(-3))' subgroup. He then uses them to split M, M^!, M^!_0 and the normalisers as semidirect products.
errors: (137)–(138) are stated, not proved. The splitting relies on the previous page's claim that the map from L_0^{Pi_0} to N^*_sigma is trivial.
The claim M^! ≅ M^!_0 × mu needs mu central and not contained in M^!_0. This is consistent with the index-2 statement, but the page does not check it.
The notation is unstable: '!' and 'α' are mixed up, both N^{*!}_{σ0} and N^{*!}_{σ,0} appear, and the gamma/Gamma conventions shift. The derivation in (141) is a sketch ('Ainsi —' breaks off).

ideas.what: Splitting of the GT-type extension M -> Gamma_Q-tilde by the normaliser of the order-2 element, interpreted as the section at the rational point lambda = 1/2
ideas.modern_name: Galois/GT section attached to a non-tangential rational point (the j = 1728 point) of M_{0,4} or P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sections from rational points are classical anabelian geometry (Grothendieck's letter to Faltings, 1983). Their combinatorial GT analogues relate to Lochak–Schneps and Nakamura–Schneps (1990s), who use the order-2 and order-3 relations.
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the role of the points with extra symmetry (1/2 and e^{i pi/3}) and of the 2- and 3-torsion of the modular group, but not this construction explicitly

ideas.what: Semidirect decompositions M = M(1/2).S^+-hat, M^! = M(1/2).Pi, M^!_0 = M(1/2).Pi_0, N^*_sigma = M(1/2).L_sigma, together with the remark on which subgroups are normal
ideas.modern_name: Splitting of the outer/automorphism extension of the profinite (pure) modular or braid group by GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld, Ihara (GT acting on profinite braid groups); later Minamide–Nakamura and Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki on automorphism groups of profinite braid groups

ideas.what: Analysis of the order-3 normaliser: its section M(-J) exists only over the index-2 subgroup where the quadratic character epsilon_3 (Q(sqrt(-3))) is trivial
ideas.modern_name: GT/Galois section at the CM point lambda = e^{i pi/3} (j = 0), defined over Q(sqrt(-3))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Analogue of the Galois-theoretic fact that the point e^{i pi/3} is defined over Q(sqrt(-3)); the combinatorial GT version has no clear attribution

missed.claim: Inside the abstract GT-like group M, Grothendieck constructs combinatorial 'rational-point sections'. M(1/2) splits the full extension. M(-J) splits it only over the epsilon_3 = 1 subgroup (Q(sqrt(-3))). He uses them to give semidirect decompositions of M and its subgroups. This is a purely group-theoretic analogue of the section conjecture data for the two special points.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This bears on whether GT (or its variants) 'knows' the non-tangential rational and CM points: a GT version of the section conjecture for the points 1/2 and e^{i pi/3}. It is relevant to combinatorial anabelian geometry (Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki) and to the comparison of GT with Gal(Q-bar/Q).

missed.claim: The quadratic character epsilon_3 cuts out an index-2 subgroup Gamma' of the GT-type group as the stabiliser of the order-3 symmetric point. Thus the combinatorial structure detects the field of definition Q(sqrt(-3)) of the CM point j = 0.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests an intrinsic GT-theoretic definition of 'fields of definition' of special points. This could be compared with the cyclotomic character and the GT-analogues of quadratic characters.

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds a coherent, apparently unpublished construction: GT-type sections attached to the symmetric points 1/2 and e^{i pi/3}, with the Q(sqrt(-3)) subtlety, and the resulting semidirect splittings. Each ingredient is natural to specialists and partly echoed in Lochak–Schneps-style work. So it is a notable detail, not a surprise.
transcription_corrections: Margin note reads 'NB on a M^!_0 ⥲ M^!_{0,3}' (isomorphism of M^!_0 onto M^!_{0,3}).
'on aura donc que M(1/2) est un {+groupe+} — restriction...' is probably 'M(1/2) est une section [de] N^*_σ extension de γ_{ρ,σ} par L_σ'.
'et on a = [?] doubles [?]' is probably 'et on a des décompositions en produits semi-directs' (cf. next page '½ direct').
In (141) the formula is probably 'α v / u' i.e. αv ∈ M(0)·... ; and 'u(ρ) = i_{-1}(α)(ρ^{ε_3})' (the [?] is likely i_{-1}(α) or int(α)).
'u(ρ) doit avoir [?] une image dans S_3' is probably 'u(ρ) doit avoir même image dans S_3 = S^{+^}/Π^ que ρ'.
The final line is probably 'α est l'élément α(u) associé à u et v = α^{-1}u est l'image de u dans N^*_ρ'.
